title: What Did They Say?
description: Menyampaikan kembali apa yang dikatakan atau ditanyakan orang lain dengan reported speech. Kamu akan belajar backshift (perubahan tense), perubahan pronoun serta kata keterangan waktu dan tempat, reported questions, perbedaan say dan tell, dan kosakata untuk berita dan gosip.
objectives: Mengubah direct speech menjadi reported statements dengan backshift yang tepat
Menyesuaikan pronoun serta kata keterangan waktu dan tempat dalam reported speech
Melaporkan pertanyaan yes/no dan wh- dengan susunan kata yang benar
Memakai say, tell, dan reporting verbs lain untuk menyampaikan berita dan gosip

lessons.title: Reported Statements and Backshift
lessons.summary: Menyampaikan kembali ucapan orang lain dengan said (that) dan memundurkan tense (backshift).
objectives: Membedakan direct speech dan reported speech
Menerapkan backshift: present → past, present perfect/past simple → past perfect, will → would, can → could
Mengubah pronoun sesuai sudut pandang pelapor
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Direct speech vs reported speech
**Direct speech** mengutip kata-kata persis seseorang dengan tanda kutip: *"I'm tired," said Nadia.* **Reported speech** (indirect speech) menceritakan kembali isi ucapan itu tanpa tanda kutip: *Nadia said (that) she was tired.* We use reported speech all the time when we pass on news, messages and gossip.

### Backshift: tense mundur satu langkah
Kalau reporting verb-nya berbentuk past (*said*, *told*), tense dalam ucapan asli biasanya **mundur satu langkah ke masa lalu**. This change is called **backshift**.

| Direct speech | Reported speech |
|---|---|
| present simple: "I **work** here." | past simple: he said he **worked** there |
| present continuous: "I'**m studying**." | past continuous: she said she **was studying** |
| present perfect: "I'**ve finished**." | past perfect: he said he **had finished** |
| past simple: "I **saw** it." | past perfect: she said she **had seen** it |
| will: "I'**ll call** you." | would: he said he **would call** me |
| can: "I **can** swim." | could: she said she **could** swim |

*Am/is/are* menjadi *was/were*. Past perfect sudah kamu pelajari di Unit 2, jadi sekarang kamu bisa memakainya untuk melaporkan ucapan.

### Pronoun juga berubah
Pronoun disesuaikan dengan siapa yang berbicara sekarang. *"I love **my** job," said Ari.* → *Ari said that **he** loved **his** job.* Always ask yourself: who said it, and who am I talking to now?

### That boleh dihilangkan
Kata **that** setelah *said* bersifat opsional: *She said (that) she was busy.* Both forms are correct and very common.

### Kapan backshift tidak wajib?
- If the reporting verb is in the present (*says*, *has said*), we keep the original tense: *Dina says she is busy.*
- If the information is **still true** now, backshift is optional: *He said he lives in Port Selwyn* (dan dia memang masih tinggal di sana).
- Past simple → past perfect juga sering tidak diubah dalam percakapan santai.

Namun di level B1, gunakan backshift sebagai **aturan standar**, terutama kalau ucapan itu terjadi cukup lama yang lalu atau situasinya sudah berubah. In the exercises, follow the standard rule.

### Tips untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia
Bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah kata kerja: *Dia bilang dia capek.* In English, the verb usually changes: *She said she **was** tired.* Ingat, *was* di sini tidak berarti "dulu" — it simply follows the past reporting verb *said*.

was studying

questions.explanation: Setiap tense mundur satu langkah: is → was, are watching → were watching, has finished → had finished, will → would, can → could. This is the backshift table you should memorise.

questions.cue: Begin with: Pak Darto said that he ...
answers: Pak Darto said that he had lost his wallet
Pak Darto said he had lost his wallet

questions.context: When I met Ayu two years ago, she said, "I can speak three languages, and I'm learning Korean."

questions.text: Ayu said that she ___ speak three languages and that she ___ learning Korean.
questions.explanation: *Can* → **could**, dan *am learning* → **was learning**. Ucapan terjadi dua tahun lalu, so we use backshift for both verbs.

lessons.title: Changing Pronouns, Time and Place Words
lessons.summary: Menyesuaikan pronoun serta kata keterangan waktu dan tempat (today, tomorrow, here, this) dalam reported speech.
objectives: Mengubah today, tomorrow, yesterday, next week, ago dalam reported speech
Mengubah here, this, dan these sesuai sudut pandang baru
Menerapkan tiga langkah: tense, pronoun, waktu/tempat
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Mengapa kata keterangan waktu berubah?
When we report speech later, the time and place are often different. Kalau Bayu berkata pada hari Senin *"I'll finish it tomorrow"*, lalu kamu menceritakannya pada hari Jumat, kata *tomorrow* tidak lagi tepat — dari sudut pandang hari Jumat, tomorrow adalah hari Sabtu! So we change it to **the next day** or **the following day**.

### Tabel perubahan
| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| now | then / at that time |
| today | that day |
| tonight | that night |
| tomorrow | the next day / the following day |
| yesterday | the day before / the previous day |
| next week / month / year | the following week / the next week |
| last week / month / year | the week before / the previous week |
| two days ago | two days before / two days earlier |
| here | there |
| this (book) | that (book) |
| these (shoes) | those (shoes) |

### Pronoun dan possessive
Jangan lupa mengubah pronoun dan possessive adjective sesuai sudut pandang. *"I left **my** bag **here**," said Sinta.* → *Sinta said that **she** had left **her** bag **there**.* Notice that three things change at the same time: the tense, the pronouns and the place word.

### Langkah-langkah (step by step)
1. Change the **tense** (backshift).
2. Change the **pronouns** and possessives (I → he/she, my → his/her, we → they, our → their).
3. Change **time and place** words if the time or place is different now.

### Kapan tidak perlu diubah?
If you report something on the same day and in the same place, you don't need to change *today* or *here*: pagi ini Tom berkata "I'm busy today", lalu siang ini kamu bisa bilang *Tom said he was busy today.* Gunakan logika: apakah waktunya masih sama? In the exercises in this unit, assume the words were spoken at a different time and place unless the context says otherwise.

### Hati-hati dengan *ago*
*Ago* dihitung dari **sekarang**, jadi dalam reported speech biasanya berubah menjadi **before** atau **earlier**: *"I moved here three years ago."* → *He said he had moved there three years before.* Hal yang sama berlaku untuk *now*: gunakan *then* atau *at that time*.

lessons.title: Reported Questions
lessons.summary: Melaporkan pertanyaan yes/no dengan if/whether dan pertanyaan wh- dengan susunan kata kalimat berita.
objectives: Melaporkan pertanyaan yes/no dengan asked + if/whether
Melaporkan pertanyaan wh- dengan susunan subject + verb
Menghilangkan do/does/did dan tanda tanya dalam reported questions
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Dari pertanyaan menjadi kalimat berita
When we report a question, the result is **not a question any more**. Tidak ada tanda tanya, dan susunan katanya kembali menjadi **subject + verb** (statement word order). The most common reporting verbs are **ask**, **want to know** and **wonder**.

### 1. Yes/no questions → if / whether
| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| "**Are you** busy?" | She asked **if I was** busy. |
| "**Do you** like jazz?" | He asked **whether I liked** jazz. |
| "**Have you** finished?" | They asked **if I had** finished. |
| "**Can you** drive?" | She asked **if I could** drive. |

*If* dan *whether* artinya sama di sini ("apakah"). *Whether* is a little more formal.

### 2. Wh- questions → question word + subject + verb
| Direct | Reported |
|---|---|
| "Where **do you live**?" | He asked where **I lived**. |
| "What **are you doing**?" | She asked what **I was doing**. |
| "Why **did you leave**?" | They asked why **I had left**. |
| "When **will you arrive**?" | He wanted to know when **I would arrive**. |

### Aturan penting
- **Hilangkan do/does/did.** These auxiliaries only make direct questions. In reported questions the main verb carries the tense: *"Where do you work?"* → *She asked where I **worked**.*
- **Subject sebelum verb.** *He asked where **was I** going* ✗ → *He asked where **I was** going* ✓.
- **Tanpa tanda tanya.** The reported question is part of a statement, so it ends with a full stop.
- **Backshift** tetap berlaku seperti pada reported statements, termasuk perubahan pronoun dan kata waktu.
- *Ask* bisa langsung diikuti orang: *She **asked me** if...* (bukan *asked to me*). *Want to know* tidak diikuti orang: *He wanted to know where I lived.*

### Bandingkan dengan bahasa Indonesia
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita cukup memakai *apakah* atau kata tanya: *Dia bertanya apakah saya sibuk. Dia bertanya di mana saya tinggal.* English works in a similar way: *if/whether* = *apakah*. The difficult part for Indonesian speakers is the **word order** and removing *do/did*, so practise these two points carefully.

examples.id: Hana ingin tahu kapan bus berikutnya akan berangkat.

He asked where I lived. (tanpa do)
Artinya sama (apakah); whether sedikit lebih formal.

questions.explanation: Dalam reported question, subject datang sebelum verb: **where I was going**, bukan *where was I going*.

questions.context: "Did you finish the report?" my manager asked me.
questions.prompt: Complete the reported question.
questions.text: My manager asked me ___ I ___ the report.

whether
had finished
'd finished
finished
questions.explanation: Yes/no question → **if/whether**. *Did* dihilangkan; past simple biasanya mundur menjadi past perfect: **had finished** (past simple *finished* juga diterima).

lessons.title: Say, Tell and Other Reporting Verbs
lessons.summary: Membedakan say dan tell, serta memakai explain, mention, reply, dan ask dengan pola yang benar.
objectives: Membedakan pola say (that) dan tell + orang (that)
Memakai ungkapan tetap dengan tell dan say (tell the truth, say goodbye)
Memakai explain, mention, dan reply sebagai reporting verbs
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Say vs tell: arti mirip, pola berbeda
Keduanya berarti "berkata/mengatakan", tetapi polanya berbeda. The key question is: **is the listener (a person) mentioned directly after the verb?**

| Verb | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **say** | say (that) + clause | She **said** (that) she was busy. |
| **say** | say something **to** someone | He **said** goodbye **to** us. |
| **tell** | tell **someone** (that) + clause | She **told me** (that) she was busy. |
| **tell** | tell someone something | He **told us** the news. |

Jadi: **tell + orang**, sedangkan **say** tidak langsung diikuti orang. *She said me* ✗ / *She told me* ✓ / *She said to me* ✓ (possible, but *told me* is more common in reported statements).

### Ungkapan tetap dengan tell dan say
Some expressions always use one of the two verbs:
- **tell**: tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time, tell the difference
- **say**: say hello/goodbye, say sorry, say yes/no, say a word, say something/nothing

Contoh: *Please **tell** me the truth.* / *He left without **saying** goodbye.* Ungkapan ini sebaiknya dihafal sebagai satu paket (chunk).

### Reporting verbs lain
Agar ceritamu lebih hidup, pakai kata kerja lain selain *say* dan *tell*:

| Verb | Pattern | Example |
|---|---|---|
| explain | explain (to someone) that... | She **explained to us** that the road was closed. |
| mention | mention (to someone) that... | He **mentioned** that he was moving. |
| reply | reply that... | I **replied** that I was fine. |
| ask | ask (someone) if / wh-... | They **asked me** where I lived. |

Perhatikan: *explain* dan *mention* polanya seperti *say*, bukan *tell*, jadi tidak boleh langsung diikuti orang. *He explained me* ✗ → *He explained **to me*** ✓ or *He explained* (without a person) ✓.

### Ringkasan cepat
If there is a person right after the verb, use **tell** (or *ask*). If there isn't, use **say**, *explain*, *mention* or *reply*. Kalau ragu, cek: apakah ada *me, him, her, us, them, Rina...* tepat setelah kata kerjanya? If yes, you need *tell*.

examples.en: Fajar told us that he had found a new job.
examples.id: Fajar memberi tahu kami bahwa dia sudah mendapat pekerjaan baru.

examples.en: Fajar said that he had found a new job.
examples.id: Fajar berkata bahwa dia sudah mendapat pekerjaan baru.

examples.en: Grandpa told the children a story about the old harbour.
examples.id: Kakek menceritakan sebuah kisah kepada anak-anak tentang pelabuhan tua itu.

examples.en: The guide explained to us that the museum was closed on Mondays.
examples.id: Pemandu menjelaskan kepada kami bahwa museum itu tutup setiap hari Senin.

examples.en: She left the party without saying goodbye.
examples.id: Dia meninggalkan pesta tanpa berpamitan.

vocabulary.example: I always tell the truth to my parents.
He told a lie about his age.
The teacher explained that the test would be online.
Did she mention that she was moving to Port Selwyn?
He replied that he was too busy to come.
My uncle always tells funny jokes at dinner.

grammar.pattern: say (that) + clause / say something to someone
tell + person (+ that) + clause / tell + person + something
grammar.example: He told me (that) he was late.
She explained to me that the shop was closed.
grammar.note: Polanya seperti say: pakai to sebelum orang.

mistakes.wrong: My cousin said me that she was getting married.
mistakes.right: My cousin told me that she was getting married.
mistakes.why: Jika ada orang langsung setelah kata kerja, pakai tell (atau said to me).

mistakes.wrong: He told that he was tired.
mistakes.right: He said that he was tired.
mistakes.why: Tell memerlukan orang setelahnya; tanpa orang, pakai say.

mistakes.wrong: The guide explained us the rules.
mistakes.right: The guide explained the rules to us.
mistakes.why: Explain tidak langsung diikuti orang; gunakan explain something to someone.
Ungkapan tetapnya adalah tell the truth.

sections.summary: Use **tell + person** (*She told me...*) and **say** without a person (*She said...*) or **say to + person**. Hafalkan ungkapan tetap: *tell the truth/a lie/a story/a joke* dan *say hello/goodbye/sorry*. *Explain* dan *mention* polanya seperti say: *explain to someone*.

reviewCards.front: She ___ me that she was busy. (say/tell)
reviewCards.back: told — tell + person
said — tanpa orang setelah verb
tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke
say hello/goodbye, say sorry, say yes/no
He explained to me ... ✓

questions.prompt: Raka ___ me that the meeting was cancelled.
questions.explanation: Ada orang (*me*) langsung setelah kata kerja, jadi kita butuh **told**. *Said*, *explained* and *spoke* cannot be followed directly by a person.
questions.misconception: Said me ✗ — say tidak langsung diikuti orang.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with words from the bank.
questions.text: Mrs. Wulan ___ the class a funny story, and then she ___ that the test was on Friday.
answers: told
said
questions.explanation: *Tell* + orang + something: **told the class a story**. Setelah itu tidak ada orang sebelum *that*, jadi pakai **said**.

questions.prompt: Write ONE word to complete the sentence: "Please ___ me the truth. Did you break the vase?"
answers: tell
questions.explanation: Ungkapan tetapnya adalah **tell the truth** (berkata jujur), dan ada orang (*me*) setelah kata kerja.

questions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
questions.explanation: *Say* tidak boleh langsung diikuti orang. Use **told me** (or *said to me*).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb for each gap.
questions.text: Nobody believes Fajar because he often ___ lies. Yesterday he ___ that he had met a famous singer at the airport.
questions.explanation: Ungkapan tetap: **tell lies** (berbohong). Gap kedua tidak ada orang sebelum *that*, jadi pakai **said**.

questions.prompt: Correct the mistake in the sentence.
questions.sentence: The guide explained us that the museum was closed.
answers: The guide explained to us that the museum was closed
The guide explained to us the museum was closed
The guide explained that the museum was closed
The guide told us that the museum was closed
The guide told us the museum was closed
questions.explanation: *Explain* tidak langsung diikuti orang. Correct forms: **explained to us that...**, **explained that...**, or use *told us that...*.

lessons.title: Passing On News and Gossip
lessons.summary: Menyampaikan berita, pesan, dan gosip dengan reported speech serta kosakata seperti rumour, announce, admit, dan apparently.
objectives: Menggunakan kosakata berita dan gosip (rumour, announce, admit, deny, apparently)
Menggabungkan reported statements, reported questions, dan say/tell dalam percakapan
Bereaksi secara alami terhadap berita yang disampaikan orang lain
lessons.completionCriteria: Baca semua bagian materi dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.

sections.explanation:
### Membicarakan berita dan gosip
In everyday conversation we often pass on information from other people: news from the TV, a message from a colleague, or a bit of gossip about a neighbour. Di pelajaran ini kamu menggabungkan semua yang sudah dipelajari — backshift, kata waktu, reported questions, dan say/tell — untuk bercerita secara natural.

### Kosakata penting
| Word | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| gossip | gosip, obrolan tentang orang lain | Don't believe all the gossip at work. |
| rumour | kabar burung, desas-desus | There's a rumour that the shop is closing. |
| announce | mengumumkan | The school announced that the exams would start in May. |
| admit | mengakui | He admitted that he had made a mistake. |
| deny | menyangkal | She denied that she had read my diary. |
| apparently | katanya, rupanya | Apparently, Mr. Fadli is leaving. |
| according to | menurut | According to the news, it will rain all week. |

### Frasa untuk menyampaikan kabar
- *Guess what! Ayu **told me** that she **was getting** married.*
- *Have you heard? **Apparently**, the café on Maple Street **is closing**.*
- ***According to** the newspaper, the new bridge **will** open in June.*
- *I **heard that** Dimas **had won** a prize.*

Catatan: *apparently* dan *according to* biasanya diikuti **kalimat biasa tanpa backshift**, karena tidak ada reporting verb past di depannya. Backshift happens after past reporting verbs like *said, told, announced, admitted, denied*.

### Bereaksi terhadap berita (reacting to news)
When someone tells you news or gossip, react naturally:
- Surprise: *Really? / No way! / I don't believe it!*
- Good news: *That's great news! / Good for her!*
- Bad news: *Oh no, that's terrible. / What a shame.*
- Checking: *Who told you that? / Are you sure?*

Reaksi singkat seperti ini membuat percakapan terdengar alami dan menunjukkan bahwa kamu mendengarkan.

### Hati-hati dengan gosip
Rumours are not always true. Bahasa Inggris punya cara sopan untuk menunjukkan bahwa kita belum yakin: *I'm not sure it's true, but...*, *Apparently...*, *Someone told me that...*. Using these phrases shows that you are only passing on information, not claiming it is a fact. Ini penting, terutama di tempat kerja.

examples.en: Apparently, the bakery on Cedar Road is closing next month.
examples.id: Katanya, toko roti di Cedar Road akan tutup bulan depan.

examples.en: The company announced that it would hire fifty new workers.
examples.id: Perusahaan itu mengumumkan bahwa mereka akan merekrut lima puluh pekerja baru.

examples.en: Yudi admitted that he had forgotten my birthday.
examples.id: Yudi mengakui bahwa dia lupa ulang tahun saya.

examples.en: According to my sister, the new teacher is very strict.
examples.id: Menurut kakak saya, guru baru itu sangat tegas.

examples.en: Guess what! Rina told me she was moving to Port Selwyn.
examples.id: Coba tebak! Rina memberi tahu saya bahwa dia akan pindah ke Port Selwyn.

vocabulary.example: My neighbours love to gossip about everyone on our street.
There's a rumour that our manager is leaving.
The airline announced that the flight was delayed.
She admitted that she had broken the printer.
He denied that he had taken the money.
Apparently, there will be a new park near the station.
According to the weather report, it will be sunny tomorrow.

grammar.note: Polanya seperti say: tidak langsung diikuti orang.
Tidak ada reporting verb past, jadi tidak perlu backshift.

grammar.example: I heard that Dimas had won a prize.
grammar.note: Heard juga past, jadi tense biasanya mundur.

mistakes.wrong: According to me, the film was boring.
mistakes.right: In my opinion, the film was boring.
mistakes.why: According to dipakai untuk sumber informasi lain, bukan untuk pendapat sendiri.

mistakes.wrong: The school announced us that the trip was cancelled.
mistakes.right: The school announced that the trip was cancelled.
mistakes.why: Announce tidak langsung diikuti orang (tidak seperti tell).

mistakes.wrong: He admitted that he has broken the window.
mistakes.right: He admitted that he had broken the window.
mistakes.why: Setelah reporting verb past (admitted), present perfect berubah menjadi past perfect.

sections.summary: To pass on news and gossip, use reporting verbs like **told, said, announced, admitted, denied** with backshift, or phrases like **Apparently,** and **According to...** without backshift. Gunakan reaksi seperti *Really? / No way! / That's great news!* dan frasa hati-hati seperti *I'm not sure it's true, but...*.

reviewCards.back: kabar burung / desas-desus
admit = mengakui; deny = menyangkal
Katanya/rupanya ... — diikuti kalimat biasa, tanpa backshift
In my opinion ✓ (according to = menurut sumber lain)
Really? / No way! / I don't believe it!

questions.prompt: Have you heard the ___? People are saying that Mr. Fadli is leaving the company, but nobody knows if it's true.
questions.explanation: Informasi yang beredar dari mulut ke mulut dan belum pasti benar disebut **rumour** (kabar burung). *Nobody knows if it's true* is the key clue.

questions.prompt: Think of a piece of news a friend or family member told you recently. Report it to a partner in 4–6 sentences. Say who told you, what they said, and what they asked you. Finish with a reaction.
questions.sampleAnswer: Guess what! My cousin Dewi called me yesterday. She told me that she had passed her final exams. She said that she was going to look for a job in Port Selwyn. She also asked me if I could help her with her CV. Apparently, her parents are planning a small party for her. That's great news!
questions.explanation: Gunakan **told me that / said that** dengan backshift, **asked me if** untuk pertanyaan, dan tutup dengan reaksi alami. Speak clearly and connect your sentences with *also*, *then* and *apparently*.

questions.prompt: Choose the best reply to complete the dialogue.

dialogue.speaker: Yoga
dialogue.text: What did Maya say about the new café on Maple Street?

dialogue.speaker: Yoga
dialogue.text: Oh, maybe we can go there on Saturday, then.

options: She said it was great but quite expensive.
She said me it was great but quite expensive.
She told it was great but quite expensive.
She said that is it great but quite expensive.
questions.explanation: Hanya **She said it was great...** yang benar: *said* tanpa orang, backshift *is* → *was*, dan susunan subject + verb. *said me* dan *told it was* salah pola.

questions.prompt: At a press conference yesterday, the company ___ that it would open three new stores next year.
questions.explanation: Menyampaikan informasi resmi kepada publik = **announce** (mengumumkan). A company does not *gossip*, *chat* or *whisper* at a press conference, and *gossiped/chatted that* is not a normal pattern.

questions.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order to make a sentence.
questions.explanation: Kalimat dimulai dengan sumber (*According to the local newspaper*), lalu reporting verb (*the mayor said*) dan isi laporan dengan backshift: *would open the following spring*.

questions.prompt: Translate into English. Use told.
questions.source: Rina memberi tahu saya bahwa dia sudah pindah rumah.
answers: Rina told me that she had moved house
Rina told me she had moved house
Rina told me that she'd moved house
Rina told me she'd moved house
Rina told me that she had moved to a new house
Rina told me she had moved to a new house
Rina told me that she'd moved to a new house
Rina told me she'd moved to a new house
Rina told me that she had moved
Rina told me she had moved
Rina told me that she'd moved
Rina told me she'd moved
questions.explanation: *Memberi tahu saya* → **told me** (tell + orang). *Sudah pindah rumah* setelah reporting verb past → past perfect **had moved (house)**.

unitTestQuestions.context: "I sent the email yesterday," Pak Hendra said last week.
unitTestQuestions.prompt: Pak Hendra said that he ___ the email the day before.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Past simple *sent* mundur menjadi past perfect **had sent**, dan *yesterday* → *the day before*. *Was send* is not a correct verb form.

unitTestQuestions.context: "Can you help me with my homework?" Kevin asked me.
unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete the reported question with ONE word.
unitTestQuestions.text: Kevin asked me if I ___ help him with his homework.
answers: could
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Can* dalam reported speech berubah menjadi **could**. The question becomes statement word order: *if I could help him*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the question in reported speech.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: "Why did you leave the party early?" Mia asked me.
answers: Mia asked me why I had left the party early
Mia asked me why I'd left the party early
Mia asked me why I left the party early
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Did* dihilangkan, susunan menjadi **why I had left** (past simple → past perfect; *why I left* juga diterima). No question mark at the end.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Match Tina's words (direct speech) with the correct reported form.

pairs.right: She asked if I was hungry.
She asked what I was eating.
She said she would cook dinner.
She asked if I had eaten.

unitTestQuestions.explanation: Statement → *said* + backshift; yes/no question → *asked if*; wh- question → *asked what* + subject + verb; *will* → *would*; *have eaten* → *had eaten*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Find the incorrect part of the sentence.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Tell* harus diikuti orang (*told us/me*). Without a person, use **said**: *Yesterday Lukas said that he had found a new job.*

unitTestQuestions.source: Mira said that she was tired.
answers: Mira bilang dia lelah
Mira bilang bahwa dia lelah
Mira berkata dia lelah
Mira berkata bahwa dia lelah
Mira mengatakan dia lelah
Mira mengatakan bahwa dia lelah
Mira bilang dia capek
Mira bilang bahwa dia capek
Mira berkata bahwa dia capek
Mira mengatakan bahwa dia capek
Mira bilang dia sedang lelah
Mira berkata bahwa dia sedang lelah
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Was* di sini muncul karena backshift setelah *said*, bukan berarti "dulu". In Indonesian we simply say *Mira bilang/berkata (bahwa) dia lelah*.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Choose the best line to complete the dialogue.

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Did you call the hotel about our room?

dialogue.speaker: Nina
dialogue.text: Great, so we can leave our bags there before lunch.

options: Yes. The receptionist said that the room would be ready at ten.
Yes. The receptionist told that the room will be ready at ten.
Yes. The receptionist said me the room was ready at ten.
Yes. The receptionist asked if was the room ready at ten.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **said that the room would be ready** benar: say tanpa orang + backshift *will* → *would*. *told that* butuh orang, *said me* salah, dan *if was the room* salah susunan.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Correct the mistake in the sentence.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: He asked me what did I want for my birthday.
answers: He asked me what I wanted for my birthday
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Dalam reported question, *did* dihilangkan dan susunannya subject + verb: **what I wanted**.
